thesis: Astronomical change involved religious thinkers, mixed institutions and correction of errors, not uniform harmony or permanent war.

ideas.statement: Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler and Newton show that beliefs can motivate inquiry while models and hypotheses receive independent evaluation; nuance does not excuse coercion.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Kepler retained harmony concerns while models changed; Newton’s anti-Trinitarian theology resists generic religious appropriation, and manuscript word totals need defined corpora.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Kepler retained harmony concerns while models changed; Newton’s anti-Trinitarian theology resists generic religious appropriation, and manuscript word totals need defined corpora.

audit.notes: All batch units analyzed directly; uncertainty and counterexamples retained.
